paper_title: RLPlanner: Reinforcement Learning based Floorplanning for Chiplets with Fast Thermal Analysis

extraction.paper_title: RLPlanner: Reinforcement Learning based Floorplanning for Chiplets with Fast Thermal Analysis

scenario.description: Ascend 910 System benchmark (reference [6]) used to compare RLPlanner, RLPlanner(RND), TAP-2.5D(HotSpot) and TAP-2.5D*(Fast Thermal Model). The pinned weiweihook/RLPlanner config/Ascend910.cfg gives 6 chiplets: widths 14.5, 10.5, 7.75, 7.75, 7.75, 7.75 mm, heights 31.4, 16, 11.87, 11.87, 11.87, 11.87 mm, and powers 256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20 W. The paper and config give no final placement coordinates. The paper reports for RLPlanner: reward -7.4063, wirelength 18130 mm, maximum temperature 77.12 C, runtime 7773 s.
scenario.architecture: 2.5D chiplet-based system (Huawei Ascend 910), 6 chiplets on an interposer, per pinned config/Ascend910.cfg:1
scenario.workload: Not published in the paper; only static per-chiplet power values appear in the pinned config
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state maximum temperature of 77.12 C (RLPlanner, Table I) with per-chiplet powers 256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20 W from config/Ascend910.cfg; original solver HotSpot with the fast LTI thermal model; optimizer PPO reinforcement learning with RND bonus; benchmark baselines TAP-2.5D (simulated annealing)

original_setup.solver: Ground truth is the open-source HotSpot thermal solver. RLPlanner's reward loop uses its own fast thermal model, a physics-informed linear time-invariant (LTI) thermal resistance network with self-thermal and mutual-thermal resistance tables characterized from HotSpot runs (Table II: MAE 0.2523 K, 127x speed-up vs HotSpot). TAP-2.5D(HotSpot) baseline uses HotSpot directly.
original_setup.optimizer: RLPlanner: proximal policy optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning that places chiplets sequentially, with an action mask and a shared CNN encoder for policy and value heads. The RLPlanner(RND) variant adds a random network distillation exploration bonus. Reward is -lambda*W - mu*smoothed penalty on max(T-T0,0). Baselines are TAP-2.5D (simulated annealing) with HotSpot or with the fast thermal model.
original_setup.controller: None. There is no runtime thermal or power controller. The RL agent is a design-time floorplanning policy, and the chiplet powers are static values from the pinned config/Ascend910.cfg (256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20 W).
original_setup.benchmark: Ascend 910 System (paper reference [6]), a 6-chiplet 2.5D system, from the Table I Ascend 910 column. Chiplet widths, heights and powers are in the pinned weiweihook/RLPlanner config/Ascend910.cfg. Compared methods: RLPlanner, RLPlanner(RND), TAP-2.5D(HotSpot), TAP-2.5D*(Fast Thermal Model). RLPlanner row: reward -7.4063, wirelength 18130 mm, runtime 7773 s.

thermal_observable.location: Maximum operating temperature of the chiplet-based Ascend 910 system for the final RLPlanner floorplan (Table I, Ascend 910 column, RLPlanner row). The exact location of the hotspot is not published.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum over the system (peak temperature), a single steady-state value per method. Table I does not state whether it is a HotSpot or fast-model value, nor the averaging method.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper's 77.12 degC is a peak temperature for an RL-optimized final placement that is not published, so it cannot be reproduced or numerically compared with a separately generated illustrative placement.

The original thermal evaluation uses HotSpot and an LTI self/mutual-resistance fast model for 2.5D chiplets on an interposer. The interposer, package, heat-spreader and cooling parameters are not given in the paper or pinned config, so the original cooling boundary conditions cannot be matched.

The original method is an RL floorplanner (PPO plus RND) that co-optimizes wirelength and temperature with microbump assignment. A thermal-only Studio run has no optimizer, wirelength or microbump assignment, so that part cannot be replicated.

The paper's workload is a static steady-state power per chiplet, with no transient behaviour, power time series, controller or reliability analysis. Any one-row power trace is a steady-state surrogate only.
The paper's fast thermal model is an LTI approximation with a reported MAE of about 0.25 K vs HotSpot. A different solver will differ in numerical details.
The system is 2.5D (chiplets on an interposer), not 3D stacked, so no vertical stacking mismatch applies. Any Studio 2D model must still represent the interposer layer.
Final chiplet coordinates are not supplied by the reference files; generated shelf positions illustrate a 2D power snapshot, not the published placement.

methods.note: Page 1 Fig. 1 text and page 2 Sec. II-B/II-C support PPO, an RND bonus, a shared CNN encoder with separate heads, an action mask, microbump assignment before thermal evaluation, and a HotSpot-characterized LTI self/mutual-resistance fast model. The reward formula is garbled in pdftotext, so the exact form of the smoothing term was not verified. The paper does not say how the Ascend 910 Table I temperature was computed (HotSpot or fast model).

code.note: The paper only says 'More details can be found at the github', with no URL, commit or placement output. The only repository evidence is one pinned config file. No RLPlanner code, fast-model tables or final Ascend 910 placement was inspected. The generated shelf layout is not from the source code.

parameters.note: Reward hyperparameters (lambda, mu, T0, alpha), the PPO/RND settings and the self/mutual resistance tables are not in the supplied evidence. The config widths, heights and powers are present, but the config states no units (mm and W are assumed), and the paper never lists chiplet dimensions or powers for the Ascend 910 case. The reference [6] article was not inspected. Reference [6] is not a pinned asset, so the dimension and power provenance is unverified.

config.note: There is no HotSpot configuration: interposer size and thickness, package layers, materials, heat sink or cooling boundary, ambient temperature and grid resolution are all absent. The Studio package and material assumptions are also not provided. The generated custom_2d_steady experiment has no interposer or cooling definition, so it cannot be matched to the paper's thermal setup. The config's path 'outputs/case6/' and comment '#ascend910' only weakly tie it to the Table I Ascend 910 column.

data.note: All six blocks have same-scenario powers (256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20 W) and dimensions from the pinned config, but with an assumed unit and only index-based block names. The final placement is unpublished, so the shelf coordinates are illustrative and not the paper's result. The Table I values (77.12 degC, -7.4063, 18130, 7773) come only from pdftotext output, with ambiguous column layout and no visual verification of the table. The constant power row is a steady-state surrogate, not a published trace.

assessment.summary: Scenario: RLPlanner (W4390437658), Ascend 910 System, 6 chiplets on a 2.5D interposer. The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, and the Studio run did run (run_kind custom_2d_steady, status completed, run id c9e576d2499d413c90191897c6ed8b9b). The input gate passed with no input errors, so the deterministic gate allowed an exploratory run. The scientific gate failed, independently_verified is false, and comparison_valid is false. Inputs: widths, heights and powers (256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20 W) come from pinned weiweihook/RLPlanner config/Ascend910.cfg at commit a75abf0b167a316dc5e2dd8b8d3d926114039271. The placement is a generated deterministic shelf layout, not the published RL floorplan, which is unavailable. Units (mm, W) are assumed because the config does not state them. A custom 2D steady run has no transient trace; the input.ptrace is one constant row of source powers, so only a steady-state snapshot is represented. Studio result: with bundled example.materials and package.config, the hottest block was chiplet_1 at 382.38 K (109.23 C). Other chiplets ranged from 88.29 C (chiplet_4) to 98.22 C (chiplet_5). A +1 W perturbation on chiplet_1 raised it to 382.59 K (about +0.21 K), so the model responds plausibly and the sensitivity check passed. Comparison to the paper: the paper's 77.12 C is a system-wide peak for an unpublished RL-optimized placement, with unknown HotSpot or fast-model origin and unknown cooling boundaries. The Studio 109.23 C is a block-level steady temperature for a generated placement under bundled package assumptions. The location, aggregation, placement and boundary assumptions do not match, so the roughly 32 C difference is not a numerical agreement or disagreement and must not be read as replication or refutation. Only qualitative inference is supported: the 256 W chiplet dominates the thermal behavior, and the generated layout, which stacks it next to other chiplets, and the unspecified cooling strongly influence peak temperature. This is an exploratory, illustrative result and not an exact replication of the paper.
